General Ketheric Thorm[5] is an Undead with elven ancestry and appearance,[4] the Chosen of  Myrkul, and one of the leaders of the enigmatic Cult of the Absolute. He serves as one of the main antagonists in Baldur's Gate 3.
“
Our darling will live again. What kind of man would I be if I didn't raze the world entire for her sake?
„
— Ketheric Thorm in a diary entry

Overview

Once the governor of Reithwin Town, personal tragedy, loss and grief drove him down the path of darkness and violence, the eventual result of which was his defeat in battle a century ago by the combined forces of the Harpers and druids of the Emerald Grove. Now, risen from the grave to lead the Absolute's forces as their general, he seeks to destroy Baldur's Gate, spread the cult of the Absolute, and have his daughter  Isobel with him once again.

Background

Risen from the grave a hundred years after the events that led to his downfall, Ketheric Thorm serves as the main antagonist of Act Two of the game, after being introduced during Act One through dialogue and in-game notes first. As the party members search for ways to cure their tadpole situation, many clues point towards Moonrise Towers and Ketheric himself and the party eventually must bring him down in order to rid the Shadow-Cursed Lands from its curse.

By exploring Moonrise Towers, through subsequent battle with him, and later exploring the Illithid colony under the stronghold, an elaborate conspiracy behind the tadpoles in the party members's heads is unveiled. Ketheric's alliance with  Enver Gortash and  Orin the Red is also exposed, along with his plans to secure all three Netherstones for himself.[6] Also, during the fight against him it is revealed that it was  Myrkul who brought Ketheric back from the dead.

Gameplay

  • Ketheric Thorm is a level 11 Undead boss who retains some features of his past life, and is one of the main antagonists in the game.
  • He can be found throughout Act Two, while being referenced through dialogue and notes in Act One.
  • Fighting him is required in order to obtain his Netherstone and proceed with the story.
  • In combat, he is most similar to an Oathbreaker paladin,[7] able to cast a form of Smite with his attacks, as well as having access to Aura spells and able to raise Undead minions.
  • Despite his status as a boss, Ketheric can still be disarmed, knocked prone or affected by other types of weapon abilities.
  • True to his skill as a general, Ketheric commands his allies to focus their attacks on targets he deems especially troublesome via Deadly Orders.
  • The outcome of the quests relating to the  Nightsong, as well as dialogue checks, can influence the encounters with him.

Description

Appearance

Ketheric has a severe, weathered look - his face marked by age and a permanent scowl. He wears a plain circlet adorned with the skull of Myrkul, and a richly detailed suit of armor which clearly identifies him as the Chosen of the Lord of Bones. His Netherstone rests securely in an ornate golden cage on his chest armour. Ketheric's straight gray hair is tucked neatly behind his slightly pointed ears. A thick, full beard connects to his hair, which suggests he has only partly elven ancestry (according to the Forgotten Realms lore elves, unlike half-elves, cannot grow facial hair).[8]

Despite this, in the first vision imposed upon the party by the  Absolute near the Goblin Camp, the Narrator calls him "a mighty elf" among the Chosen Three. The  Elder Rothé in Grymforge, if spoken to via  Speak with Animals, also describes him in the same words. Companions' comments on murals surrounding Isobel's grave inside the Thorm Mausoleum (where the key points of Ketheric's story are depicted), too, refer to him as an elf.

Presumably, Ketheric was first planned to be an Elf but was later changed to half-elf, and the (likely) erroneous mentionings as an elf are oversights by the developers.[9]

Personality

Though best described as a man tormented and utterly transformed by grief[10], his daughter  Isobel speaks of a loving, doting father while she was growing up, one who had the admiration of his subjects for being just and fair, full of love for his wife who he adored more than anyone else. Tragedy, however, would turn him into a bitter, wrathful man, willing to cleanse Reithwin from any Selûnites to spite the  Moonmaiden for abandoning him.

Whatever the man he once was, the Ketheric the party encounters is a callous one, evident by his dismissal of  Minthara and the goblins, ordering their torture and execution for failing him. Though courteous when needed, he will quickly condemn the party to death should they defy his orders. Above all, however, he is ruthless and relentless [11] in his pursuits, willing to burn the entire world just to be reunited with his daughter.[12]

Though his loss and anguish moved him to change his patron god twice in search of relief, he proved to be an ardent believer of each while serving them: for Selûne, he built Moonrise Towers in her honour, for  Shar, he built a grand temple under town in her name and for  Myrkul, he amassed a great army ready to raze Baldur's Gate to the ground.

Through it all, he kept  a note from Isobel close to him, showing that deep down a small part of him still remembers the man he once was.

History

“
I pity you. Truly.
„
— Isobel, addressing a bust of Ketheric Thorm while in her quarters at the Last Light Inn

Governor of Reithwin

A devout worshipper of  Selûne, Thorm lived with his wife  Melodia and daughter  Isobel near the town of Reithwin as governor of the region. Such was his devotion to the Moonmaiden that he would commission a local mason,  Morfred, to construct a grand bastion in her honour: Moonrise Towers.

Yet disaster struck the Thorm family when Melodia passed away, leaving Ketheric to raise their daughter alone.[13] With a child in his care, Ketheric persevered, and though doubts plagued his mind, he kept the Selûnite ways. As Isobel grew older, their happy years had a sour note: he disapproved of a budding relationship between his daughter and an immortal Aasimar visiting the town,  Dame Aylin, daughter of Selûne.

The conflict would be cut short, however, as tragedy would befall Ketheric once more, and his daughter Isobel passed away.[14]

Conversion to Shar

Grief-stricken and unable to cope with his loss, Ketheric Thorm renounced the worship of the  Moonmaiden and turned to  Shar, the Lady of Loss.[15][16]

Moonrise Towers, once a bastion of Light, turned into a symbol of darkness and grief; Thorm systematically erased all Selûnite trace of the town, forcing all believers of the Moonmaiden to convert to Shar, flee, or die.[17] Those who remained devout to Selûne did so in secret, arranging a ⁠fledgling resistance even as Sharran spies began to infiltrate their gathering places.[18]

In Ketheric's downward spiral into darkness, Shar compelled him to build an army of Dark Justiciars beneath his home town in order to cleanse the world of Light. Ketheric lured Isobel's lover, Aylin, whom he had once quarreled with under Selûne, and trapped her in a prison. He had the immortal demigod serve as a perpetual sacrifice for Dark Justiciar initiates – a design of his closest confidante, the necromancer  Balthazar.[19][20]

As terror gripped the town he had previously served so faithfully, the Harpers, a loose organization that roots out villainy, saw that Ketheric had committed "Murder, Slavery, and Desecration of Temples Most Holy." They began to seek an alliance to end his reign.[21]

Reithwin soon became the site of a wintertime battle between Ketheric's army and the combined forces of the Harpers and druids of the  Emerald Enclave.[22] Ketheric's Justiciars repelled the combined forces, and the Harpers  unsuccessfully attempted surrender. [23] All the while a  devil's bargain was struck with  Raphael beneath the town by the Selûnite-in-secret  Morfred as well as  Yurgir and his merregons; they then worked to annihilate Ketheric's Dark Justiciar army.

In the end, the Sharran army was defeated, ⁠virtually all Dark Justiciars were slain, and finally Ketheric himself perished [24]. And yet, before the final blow was struck and his defeat was sealed, he unleashed a Shadow Curse upon the land - a curse that would persist long after his demise, afflicting all battle survivors and any remaining inhabitants who did not flee. His body was later buried in the Thorm Mausoleum.

Chosen of Myrkul

“
I'll tell you a story, True Soul. About a man who sold himself piece by piece.
„
— Ketheric Thorm

More than a hundred years later, Thorm would be brought back from the dead by  Myrkul as General Ketheric Thorm. The God of Death tasked the general to form an alliance with the apostles of the other two of the Dead Three and bring death to the world, offering in payment the resurrection of Ketheric's daughter Isobel.

After reviving his daughter with help of Balthazar, Ketheric's plan at a family reunion failed: when the revived Isobel saw his broken visage, she fled into the darkness, protected by her goddess Selûne. The town had been ravaged by Ketheric's death rattle, the Shadow Curse. Looming over the town for a century, all within had either died outright from it or been twisted into horrific monsters.

Undeterred, empowered by Myrkul, and granted immortality by the Nightsong, Ketheric began amassing an army of followers of the Absolute in order to march to Baldur's Gate and sow destruction.

Tasked with the recovery of the mysterious artifact, the only object capable of thwarting the Dead Three's plans, he ultimately fails and falls at the hands of the party.[25]

Involvement

Though the party learns about Ketheric during Act 1, his involvement in the Cult of the Absolute is only explored during Act Two, allowing them to meet Ketheric himself at Moonrise Towers either before or when it's sieged.

Act Two

Moonrise Towers throne room

The party's first encounter with Ketheric Thorm starts with the general judging members of the Absolute's forces from the Goblin Camp, including  Sazza,  Fezzerk, and  Minthara if any of them are still alive. Should Minthara be alive, he sends her to the dungeons to be punished, before ordering for the goblins to be killed.

Outraged,  Drenn insults Ketheric, snatches a halberd from a guard, and hurls it into Ketheric's chest. The immortal general rips the weapon from his chest and drops it in front of Drenn, challenging and daring her to "try again". Drenn strikes him in the neck, to no avail, and he smashes Drenn's spine with his bare hands, killing her. Ketheric then leaves the hall, instructing Z'rell to leave the fate of the remaining goblins to the player character's "particular creative genius."

Ketheric moves to the rooftop of Moonrise Towers with orders not to disturb him under any circumstances. Although the party can visit him before the finale by sneaking into the rooftop, he is - if spoken with here - furious they did not wait as instructed and turns hostile. Remaining immortal at this point, he cannot be defeated.

While speaking to characters such as  Jaheira,  Z'rell, and  Balthazar, it is revealed, to some capacity, that a magical relic grants Ketheric immortality. Assisting Balthazar reveals that sometime between his life as a Sharran and his time serving Myrkul, Ketheric Thorm discovered the  Nightsong and used it to render him unkillable.

Atop Moonrise Towers

After killing or saving  Aylin, the party must confront Ketheric during the assault on Moonrise Towers. This grants the ⁠Top of the Ladder inspiration to party members with the  Noble background.

The party have the opportunity to make Ketheric see reason, by invoking  Melodia's memory, or intimidating him into submission[26]. Doing so grants the ⁠Eclipse of the Heart inspiration to party members with the  Entertainer background.

Whether or not Aylin is alive to interrupt the conversation, Ketheric concludes he has come too far to stop now and attacks the party upon discovering they have been in possession of the  Prism all along.

Once his health drops below 40%, Ketheric flees down into the Mind Flayer Colony, taking Aylin with him if she is alive.

If, however, the party chose to let Balthazar take Aylin in the Shadowfell and helped abduct Isobel, the fight at the top of the tower is skipped. Should Isobel be dead, he recounts his life story, and his sacrifices, blaming the party for her death, but not punishing them, as he wishes to keep up the façade of the Absolute's judgement. The party is instead taken prisoner in the Mind Flayer Colony, where Balthazar is tasked with transforming them into zombies and retrieving the Artefact. It is then necessary to break out of the pods and defeat Balthazar to continue.

Eventually, the party find Ketheric having a conversation with  Enver Gortash and  Orin the Red, revealing the true form of the Absolute. Gortash and Orin depart for Baldur's Gate, leaving Ketheric behind to deal with the party. Once he is defeated, the last portion of the fight will begin, this time against the  Apostle of Myrkul.

If asking Ketheric to repent by passing multiple Persuasion and / or Intimidation checks, both atop Moonrise Towers and in the Mind Flayer Colony, then the first half of his fight in the Mind Flayer Colony is skipped as he gives himself to Myrkul. Once the Apostle of Myrkul is defeated, Ketheric returns to humanoid form and mutters his daughter's name one last time before collapsing dead. After his death,  his Netherstone is taken from his corpse by the party. The inspiration ⁠Lesser of the Three is granted to party members with the  Haunted One background for killing the Apostle of Myrkul.

Combat

Main article: Ketheric Thorm/Combat

Ketheric serves as the main antagonist of Act 2 of the game and must be fought thrice in it. His defeat marks the end of the act and allows the party to proceed to their next and final destination: Baldur's Gate.
